newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada growth seen hindered by debt, cutbacks.
newsitem.headline: Canada growth seen hindered by debt, cutbacks.

text.p: Hopes that Canada's economy is headed for a rosy recovery may be too optimistic, a private research organization said in a report released on Friday.

High household debt, a low savings rate and deep public sector spending cuts are offsetting the stimulative effect of lower interest rates, especially in the two largest provinces of Ontario and Quebec, the the Conference Board of Canada said in its quarterly provincial outlook.
The board's latest provincial forecast is based on projected growth in real gross domestic product (GDP) for Canada of 2.9 percent in 1997 and 2.7 percent in 1998.
Statistics Canada reported earlier today that Canada's real GDP rose 1.5 percent in 1996 -- a figure slightly lower than most economists' projections.

"Despite the deep government spending cuts, Ontario will lead all provinces in growth in 1997, while Quebec's growth will continue to lag the national pace," said Paul Darby, the board's director of economic services.

"Manufacturing will take over from agriculture and drive growth in the Prairies, strong energy prices and investment will boost growth in Alberta, and getter prospects in forestry and mining will lift growth in B.C. this year," Darby said.
